main_body: Snow-covered conifer: a tiered cone of dark green boughs with white snow ledges on each tier and a short brown trunk at the base
top_band: At x=16 the snow on the lowest tier is rows 44-46 (L=249, then 166), above dark green boughs (L about 55). The snow ledges are lighter bands sitting above the green bough faces on each tier.
evidence: The scan shows a repeating pattern down the centre column: light snow ledge, a step of more than 100 L to dark green, then the next ledge. The snow bands are wide and foreshortened with drips below them, so they read as horizontal surfaces. The dark green boughs directly under each ledge act as shade. The ledges are thin at 2-3 rows and there is no distinct front-edge line. The reading is borderline, but it is closer to 3/4 than to a flat elevation, so it passes.

style.evidence: The candidate has 15 distinct colours and a median of 9 per tile. The references have 427-567 distinct colours and about 108 per tile, so it is far lower on both. Flat-fill coverage is 0% and the outline is tinted dark green (0% neutral), which is good. The foliage is built from a few green values in stepped bands with little per-clump leaf texture or highlights, so it looks thin and graphic next to the richly clumped Beodeul canopies. The measured density gap is too large to accept.
